properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enabled
properties.description: Master switch for the whole module. False stops every task, pass and sweep; the beans are not created at all.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.instance
properties.description: Identity written into locked_by and owner_instance columns. Defaults to the shared job-core instance identity, which keeps one pod looking like one instance across every module that claims rows.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.schedule.fixed-delay
properties.description: How often an enumeration's walk pass runs. The pass only takes scopes that are due, so this is how soon a due scope is noticed, not how often the partner is called.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.schedule.run-timeout
properties.description: How long one walk pass may hold the enumeration's run lease. A walk still in progress at the timeout stops at its checkpoint and resumes on the next pass.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.discovery.fixed-delay
properties.description: How often the scope source is paged through for scopes not yet registered. A new scope is walked at most this long after its local row appears.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.discovery.page-size
properties.description: Scopes read per page of the scope source.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.refresh.full-interval
properties.description: How often every member of a scope is listed again. Only a full walk can show that a member is gone, so this is also the longest a removal can go unnoticed.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.refresh.incremental-interval
properties.description: How often changes since a scope's watermark are fetched between full walks. Absent by default; setting it for a feed that does not declare changed-since support is refused at startup.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.walk.page-size
properties.description: Items requested per page of the feed. A page is applied in one transaction, so this is also the unit that is replayed item by item when one member fails.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.walk.max-concurrency
properties.description: Scopes walked at once by one pass.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.walk.max-scopes-per-run
properties.description: The most scopes one pass takes; the rest wait for the next. Scopes that have never completed a walk are taken first.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.sweep.confirm-after-misses
properties.description: How many consecutive completed full walks must omit a member before it is reported as having left. Use 2 for a partner that pages by offset, where an item shifting between pages mid-walk can be missed once without being gone.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.sweep.max-fraction
properties.description: The largest share of a scope's members one sweep may report without an operator. A larger sweep is withheld until confirmed or discarded through the reconciliation endpoint, because a partner answering with an empty list during an outage looks exactly like every member having been deleted. Note that a scope with a single member is always above 0.5; set 1 to switch the guard off for enumerations of very small scopes.

properties.name: ludwig.reconciliation.enumeration-defaults.retry.max-attempts
properties.description: Attempts to apply a member, or to report it as having left, before it is quarantined.

values.description: Fetch, write down, apply later. The default: per-item retry without re-calling the partner, a replayable record of what the partner said, per-record dead-lettering instead of per-run failure, and an apply cadence independent of the fetch cadence.

Apply inline, with no staging row. Cheaper and strictly worse in every failure mode - a retry re-hits the partner, and the engine's idempotency and stale-write guards are unavailable because there is no history to consult. An explicit opt-in for integrations whose data is cheap to refetch.
Count it and move on. The default: an id the partner has forgotten is a fact about the data, not an incident.
Stage a payload-less record so the reconciler's missing-record branch runs. For domains where 'gone upstream' is itself meaningful - a deactivated account, a withdrawn catalogue entry.
Treat it as a retryable failure. Correct only for a partner that returns 404 for 'not ready yet'; anywhere else this is a runaway retry loop on purpose.

hints.name: ludwig.reconciliation.tasks.keys
hints.description: Each key must match a @ReconciliationTask bean's value. The context refuses to start if a configured task has no bean, or a bean has no configuration.

values.description: One call per key, fanned out under fetch.max-concurrency. For partners with no batch endpoint.
N keys per call, sliced into chunks of fetch.batch-size. A key absent from the answer means NOT FOUND, not an error.
A catalogue walked page by page with a checkpointed cursor, joined against demand.
Submit, poll, collect against a partner that answers with a job handle. Requires a job block and job.on-ambiguous-submit.
Mark the job ORPHANED, hold its quota slot until max-lifetime, never resubmit. Correct for expensive or billable jobs: the cost of being wrong is one wasted slot and a late sync.
Start a fresh job. Correct only when a submission is cheap and genuinely idempotent on the partner's side - otherwise one crash becomes two running jobs.

Poll the job an expired lease was held for, and reclaim the slot only if it has finished or outlived its lifetime. The default, and the only setting that keeps the slot count an honest description of what the partner is doing.

Reclaim without checking. For partners with no status endpoint. Under this policy the number of jobs actually running at the partner can exceed max-concurrent, invisibly - document it where the integration is described.
